events.summary:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Maricopa County in south central Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 200 PM MST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of the Salt River below Granite Reef Dam is
imminent or occurring. Flooding of low water crossings across the
Salt River upstream of Tempe Town Lake, including McKellips Road,
is imminent or occurring.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 517 AM MST, SRP was releasing 1650 cfs from Granite Reef Dam.
Flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Salt River between Granite Reef Dam and Tempe Town Lake.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected to occur.

* WHERE...A portion of south central Colorado, including the
following areas, the Eastern San Juan Mountains, and the Upper Rio
Grande Valley.

* WHEN...From late tonight through Monday morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone location.
Rockslides will be possible in the mountainous areas. Highway 160
and Highway 17 will likely be significantly impacted by this storm.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Heavy rainfall is expected to fall Sunday and Monday across the
area, leading to elevated concerns for flooding in areas that
have recently received excessive moisture, or have recently
experienced flooding.
- The greatest risk of flooding will be along the Conejos River and
the Rio Grande, including Del Norte and Mogote.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood http://cotrip.org

events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall will be possible,
especially over the western half of San Luis Valley.

* WHERE...The western half of the San Luis Valley, including Del
Norte, Antonito and Mogote.

* WHEN...From Sunday afternoon through late Tuesday night.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone location.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Runoff from heavy rain and melting snow over the San Juan
Mountains may cause flooding in the San Luis Valley, especially
Monday and Tuesday as high flows move out of the mountains and
through the Rio Grande and Conejos River.
- The greatest risk of flooding will be along the Conejos River and
the Rio Grande, including Del Norte and Mogote.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.region: Coastal North Bay Including Point Reyes National Seashore; San Francisco Peninsula Coast
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Up to 1.5 ft of inundation above ground level is
possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways.

* WHERE...Pacific Coast.

* WHEN...Until 6 PM PDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide
is expected to be 1.5 feet above normal (7.3 ft MLLW) at 03:44
PM on Saturday 10/31. These predictions include up to 1.5 ft of
surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding
threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along
the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay,
respectively.

events.region: San Francisco; North Bay Interior Valleys; San Francisco Bay Shoreline; Northern Monterey Bay; Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Up to 1.5 ft of inundation above ground level is
possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways.

* WHERE...Bayshore locations along the San Francisco Bay, San Pablo
Bay, and Monterey Bay.

* WHEN...Until 6 PM PDT Sunday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. More substantial impacts are expected along bayshore
Marin County where increased flooding is anticipated across
low lying areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide
is expected to be 1.5 feet above normal (7.3 ft MLLW) at 03:44
PM on Saturday 10/31 and 1.0 ft above normal (6.8 ft MLLW) on
Sunday 11/01 at 3:59 PM. These predictions include up to 1.5 ft
of surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding
threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along
the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay,
respectively.
